html:
Italian Eritrea was Italy's first colony, on the Red Sea coast of the Horn of Africa, from 1890 to 1941. The map shows it in its 1938 snapshot. It is today Eritrea.

Italy took the port of Massawa in 1885 and declared the colony in 1890. Its push into Ethiopia ended in defeat at the Battle of Adwa in 1896, but Eritrea stayed Italian. The Italians built a railway from Massawa up to the highland capital, Asmara, and many Eritrean men served as askari, colonial soldiers, across Italy's wars.

Under Mussolini Eritrea became the launch pad for the invasion of Ethiopia in 1935, and in 1936 part of Italian East Africa. Asmara filled with Italian settlers and bold modernist buildings, now a World Heritage site. British forces took the colony in 1941 after the battle of Keren.
